name: How are allowances handled in luxury home construction?

mainEntity.name: How do allowances work in a high-end custom home build, and why do they cause budget overruns?
mainEntity.text: How do allowances work in a high-end custom home build, and why do they cause budget overruns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Allowances are one of the biggest budget traps in luxury construction. They are not fixed prices for the final item; they are estimates used until the owner chooses the exact product. If the allowance is too low for the level of finish desired, the project will appear affordable on paper and then climb later through upgrades and change orders. In high-end Los Angeles homes, owners should review allowance categories carefully because premium kitchens, bath fixtures, custom millwork, and specialty lighting can vary dramatically in cost. A good builder should explain how each allowance was derived, what brand or quality level it assumes, and what happens if the final selection comes in over or under that amount. The cleanest process is to make high-impact decisions early, especially for items with long lead times. That reduces budget surprises and keeps the project moving.
acceptedAnswer.description: Allowances are placeholder amounts for items not yet fully selected, such as cabinetry, fixtures, lighting, tile, and appliances. In luxury homes, unrealistic allowances are a common reason budgets rise after selections are made. The best approach is to set allowances based on actual finish levels and confirm them before construction starts.
